To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ROS are involved in plant PCD and that ROS are produced in different compartments and by different enzymes.

(i) ROS are key inducers of plant PCD, but the type of ROS, the sites of production and their interaction with other players are crucial in activating the signalling pathways triggering the different forms of plant PCD; (ii) ROS and antioxidant molecules are tightly interconnected in determining the most appropriate redox environment required by the signalling cascades that activate plant PCD.
ROS are key inducers of plant PCD, and the balance between ROS and antioxidant systems is crucial to activate specific signalling pathways leading to different forms of plant cell death.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the redox environment required to trigger plant PCD and to determine its role in plant defence responses
understanding the mechanisms of PCD in response of plants to various stimuli, with particular attention to the role of ROS in this process.
the identification of new players in the regulation of plant PCD, and the characterization of the redox environment required by these molecules for the activation of the PCD process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, in plants, PCD can be triggered by a variety of stimuli, which can activate different signalling pathways.
, in the plant PCD field, ROS are key players and that, to understand their role, the redox state of each specific cell type and/or compartment must be taken into consideration.
, in plant PCD, ROS are key molecules in determining the cell fate.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the redox status of the cell is crucial for the activation of PCD, and that ROS are involved in the regulation of the redox status, in the signalling pathways leading to the activation of PDC, and in its execution.
the redox environment of the cell, in which the PCD process is activated, plays a key role in determining the type of cell suicide.
the balance between ROS generation and removal is crucial in determining whether a cell will die or survive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the signalling pathways leading to PCD in plants involve a complex network of ROS production, scavenging and signalling molecules.
ROS and antioxidants are not only the main players of PCD in plant cells but also the main players of the redox regulation of plant development and stress response.
ROS are not only involved in the activation of PCD, but they also play a role in determining the fate of the cell undergoing this cell death.
